name: ingest
description: Records the outcome of an adapter run. Pure function over changeset.json and receipts.json. Reconciles .bead-map.json (insert/update/delete mapping records) and saves the new merkle snapshot when the run is complete. Tolerates partial receipts so unfinished operations resurface on the next emit via the idempotency path.

requirements.title: Reconcile per-op receipts
requirements.description: For every ok create receipt: insert or update the mapping record with the bead_id from the receipt and the spec_node_id from the matching create op. For every ok close receipt on a removed node: delete the mapping record. For every ok close+create pair on a modified node: update the record to point to the new bead_id. Receipts with status=error leave records unchanged.

requirements.title: Partial receipts tolerance
requirements.description: When top-level receipts status is partial (adapter stopped mid-run), ingest reconciles all ok-status ops and leaves skipped/error ops untouched. The partial state is internally consistent: successful creates have records, failed ones do not. The next spex emit recomputes against the unchanged snapshot baseline and resurfaces the unfinished work.

requirements.title: Snapshot save gated on complete status
requirements.description: spec/.snapshot.json is overwritten only when receipts.json top-level status is complete. Partial status leaves the snapshot untouched. This makes the next emit comparison pick up unfinished ops through the idempotency path.

requirements.title: Mapping consistency invariants
requirements.description: After ingest runs, the mapping store satisfies: (1) every ok create op has a record with its bead_id; (2) every ok close on a removed node has no record; (3) every modified node's close+create pair has a record pointing to the new bead_id; (4) no orphan records (spec_node_id with no live spec node in the post-apply tree); (5) no duplicate records (same spec_node_id twice); (6) snapshot saved iff complete; (7) .bead-map.json passes the bead-map schema. Ingest asserts these invariants and returns a structured error if any fails.

requirements.title: Atomic file replacement
requirements.description: Writes to .bead-map.json and spec/.snapshot.json go through a temp-file + rename pattern so a crash mid-write leaves the pre-write file intact. Never truncate in place.

requirements.title: No runtime subprocess
requirements.description: spex ingest invokes no external subprocesses. Inputs are local files (changeset.json, receipts.json); outputs are local files (.bead-map.json, spec/.snapshot.json). No tracker calls, no git calls. The invocation is declared as the api `spex ingest`, provided by IngestCommand, and the declared name is the bare invocation: `--mode refresh` selects a pathway behind that single surface rather than standing up a second one, so both modes are bound by the guarantee above and neither can drift away from it in the graph.

requirements.title: Re-run idempotency
requirements.description: Running ingest twice against the same changeset+receipts pair produces the same final state. A second run against already-reconciled receipts is a no-op: record targets already match, deletes already happened, snapshot already written. No duplication, no unexpected obsoletion.

requirements.title: Refresh mode for impl_only drift
requirements.description: Refresh mode is a parallel ingest pathway for absorbing spec drift that owes no bead work, without triggering bead lifecycle. Content modifications are never gated, whatever leaf they land on. Structural additions and removals are absorbed only for an explicitly declared allow-list: requirements and apis in either direction, additions or removals of the implementation-section leaf type, and component removals but not component additions. The first three produce no bead in either direction, so baselining one costs nothing. Components do produce beads, and a component removal is absorbable only because the orphan refusal described below still blocks the run while the bead-map holds a record for the removed node — that record must be retired first. An added component is a bead that was never created, so it is refused. Every other structural entry is refused — data_flow and test_section in either direction, because both produce beads, and the module and envelope node types, because baselining one would hide from every downstream tool a change that spex diff or spex validate rejects. RefreshHandler's absorbable table is the authoritative list; it is written out rather than derived by negation. Activation is the --mode refresh flag on spex ingest and nothing else. The pathway accepts an empty changeset and an empty receipts file, walks the current spec graph, re-hashes every content leaf, and updates each bead-map record's spec_hash to match current content (other fields untouched; records for proposal epics are skipped). A run is also refused if any bead-map record points to a spec node that no longer exists — that signals structural drift requiring the normal pipeline. After a successful refresh the bead-map and the snapshot move under one atomic commit boundary, preserving the snapshot+bead-map atomicity invariant. Same spec state plus same snapshot input always produces the same refresh output (no-op on second run, which rewrites neither file).

components.name: Reconciler
components.description: Consumes the changeset+receipts pair and applies per-op state transitions to the mapping store. Handles create (insert/update), close-on-removed (delete), close+create pairs (update to new bead_id). Asserts the seven consistency invariants before returning.

components.name: SnapshotSaver
components.description: Writes spec/.snapshot.json iff receipts top-level status is complete. Uses atomic temp-file + rename. Reads the current merkle tree via the merkle module.

components.name: IngestCommand
components.description: CLI entry point: spex ingest --changeset <file> --receipts <file> [--mode refresh]. Loads both artifacts, inspects the run mode, and dispatches: mode: normal wires Reconciler and SnapshotSaver; mode: refresh wires RefreshHandler. Returns exit 0 on success or non-zero with a structured error on any invariant violation or IO failure.

components.name: RefreshHandler
components.description: Refresh-mode ingest pathway. Consumes an empty changeset plus an empty receipts file, rebuilds the merkle tree over the current spec directory and reads each content leaf's hash off that tree rather than introducing a hashing step of its own, and updates each bead-map record's spec_hash to the current content hash (other record fields untouched; proposal-epic records are passed over). An added or removed diff entry refuses the run unless its node type is absorbable in that direction — requirement, api and implementation-section leaves in either direction, component on removal but not on addition; modified entries never reach that gate. Refuses if any bead-map record points to a spec node that no longer exists. After a successful refresh, saves the new snapshot atomically using the same write path the SnapshotSaver uses for complete-status runs, preserving the snapshot+bead-map atomicity invariant. Separated from Reconciler so the bead-lifecycle rules and the drift-absorption rules live in distinct components with distinct test surfaces.

data_flows.name: Ingest flow
data_flows.description: changeset.json + receipts.json → IngestCommand inspects the run mode → mode: normal routes through Reconciler (per-op state transitions, invariant assertion) and SnapshotSaver (writes spec/.snapshot.json iff status=complete); mode: refresh routes through RefreshHandler (re-hash every content leaf off a freshly built merkle tree, update bead-map spec_hash for changed records, save snapshot atomically, refuse on an added or removed entry outside the absorbable set). Both pathways write atomically.

apis.name: spex ingest
apis.description: Reconcile mapping records and save snapshot from a changeset+receipts pair
